_scenario: One headless Scene, no solver and no renderer. A pivot under "kinematic" authority follows an EllipticalTrajectory (center (0,1,0), radiusX 6, radiusY 3, angularVelocity 0.7, looping) through KinematicController.followPath; its child subject is "manual" and turns about +Y at 0.4 rad/s as a pure function of the step index. Three PerspectiveCameras under "constraint" authority track it: (A) an OrbitRig at distance 7 clamped to [3, 12] m and the default pitch limits, driven every step by a SeededRandom(20260813) input stream of yaw/pitch/dolly deltas, with an unlimited LookAtConstraint; (B) a world-frame FollowRig at offset (0,4,10) smoothed by a critically damped SpringDamper (2 Hz), with an unlimited LookAtConstraint; (C) a target-frame FollowRig at offset (1.5,2.5,-6) smoothed by an underdamped SpringDamper (3 Hz, zeta 0.7) under a rotated parent scaled 2x, with a LookAtConstraint slew-limited to 1.2 rad/s. A KinematicSystem at PRIORITY_KINEMATICS (400) and a ConstraintSystem at PRIORITY_CONSTRAINTS (700) share one SystemRegistry, driven 300 clean fixed steps of 1/60 s with an injected TimeState whose simulationTime is exactly step / 60. The per-step value is an FNV-1a checksum (D6) over each camera's world position and local rotation in registration order, then the subject's world position; summaryDigest is the same hasher over all 300 of them in step order.
_tier: same-runtime (§33), §33's stated initial target. The rigs call Math.sin, Math.cos, Math.acos and Math.sqrt, and SpringDamper's exact exponential step calls Math.exp — of these only sqrt is specified exactly rounded by IEEE 754, so cross-platform determinism is NOT claimed. Everything else on the path is exact: the seeded input stream is integer arithmetic, the step count and dt are fixed, iteration is insertion order, and no wall clock is read. The checksum algorithm itself is exact and cross-platform; only its inputs are runtime-bound.
